recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It restores an approved clarification that was accidentally lost and aligns the terminology page with the later FHIR-48480 warning invariant. Future work should only revisit the paragraph if the work group defines a distinct additional-binding pattern for type-scoped supplementary bindings.
issue_request: FHIR-35891 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It requested documentation that a binding on an element with multiple data types applies to all bindable types and that type-specific binding requires an explicit mechanism.
initial_application: Commit d7b4a4ab88 initially added the requested paragraph to source/terminologies.html, but ab0ada5222 removed it the next day while applying unrelated terminology edits. The current build-scope terminology source no longer contained the approved clarification before this reconciliation.
additional_context: The originating Zulip discussion and the 2022-07-18 FHIR-I minutes confirm that bindings on choice-type elements apply to all bindable types. FHIR-48480 later added a warning invariant for bindings with more than one bindable type and recommends slicing by type when the binding is not intended for every bindable type. Current ElementDefinition additional bindings do not replace the main binding, so the restored wording uses current slicing guidance for type-specific conformance bindings.
reconciliation: Added a paragraph to source/terminologies.html explaining that bindings on elements with multiple allowed types apply to all allowed bindable types: code, Coding, CodeableConcept, CodeableReference, Quantity, string, and uri. The paragraph directs authors to slice a choice element by type when a binding should apply only to a specific type.
source_changes: source/terminologies.html: Added multi-type binding guidance in the binding overview, including the current list of bindable types and type-slicing guidance for type-specific bindings.
